titel: From How to Life Forever: The Longevinauts

einzeiler: Host Mongesha explores the modern obsession with longevity, biohacking, and life…
kurzfassung: Host Mongesha explores the growing cultural and scientific obsession with longevity and biohacking as he approaches middle age. He consults television historians, astrologers, and longevity doctors like Nir Barzilai and Ron Primus to examine whether humans can realistically extend their lifespans. Along the way, family discussions and personal medical exams challenge his initial acceptance of mortality.
stichpunkte: Mongesha examines how cultural perceptions of old age have shifted since the 1980s, when fifty was portrayed as frail.
A tantric astrologer in Chennai predicts that Mongesha will pass away on July 29, 2039.
His wife Lizzie and friend Chathan strongly disagree with his passive acceptance of this predicted expiration date.
Geroscientist Nir Barzilai explains that centenarians often spend very little time sick at the end of their lives.
Doctor Ron Primus conducts a comprehensive health and lifestyle assessment, revealing that Mongesha carries significant excess visceral fat.
Primus highlights success stories where lifestyle adjustments and hyperbaric oxygen therapy reversed cognitive decline.
Mongesha reflects on his grandfather's sudden death in India and weighs the desire for extra time against the reality of mortality.

clips.text: The pursuit of extended lifespans is often criticized as an exclusive hobby for wealthy technology investors attempting to buy extra decades.
An old television advertisement for a medical alert pendant highlights how significantly daily life and technology have transformed over the decades.
Weekly conversations with trauma survivors reveal the mental challenges of listening to internal fears while discussing severe tragedies.
A theoretical milestone predicts that by 2029, medical advancements will allow humans to gain back more than one calendar year of life for every year that passes.
Optimizing personal health requires wearing biometric tracking straps, monitoring sleep data, and keeping living spaces at exactly 62 degrees.

beschreibung:
When an astrologer tells Mangesh that he’ll (probably) die early, he takes it in stride. But his family and friends (not to mention all the Don’t Die longevity influencers on his FYP) feel differently… and besides, if science can keep his brain sharp and his tennis game strong for longer, why not take advantage? So he visits Dr. Nir Barzelai, the world’s leading aging researcher, and Dr. Ron Primas, an elite longevity doctor, to figure out what he should do. Plus: A chat with Ken Reid from TV Guidance Counselor about age in pop culture, from the Golden Girls to “I’ve fallen and I can’t get up.”
Disclosure: The experts we spoke with want to be clear that although they have some minor quibbles with Bryan Johnson, they’re grateful for the fact that he’s started the conversation on longevity. Any insinuation that he’s got weird vibes is ours.
